screens.title: Single sign-on
screens.subtitle: Verify your domain, connect your identity provider, then turn it on

blocks.text: Single sign-on is part of Enterprise. Once your organization is on an Enterprise plan, you set SSO up yourself here — verify your domain, paste your identity provider’s details, and turn it on. There is no provisioning step on our side and nothing to wait for.

1. Verify your domain
Add each email domain your team signs in with. Publish the DNS record we give you, then verify — we only route a domain’s sign-ins to your identity provider once we have seen that record.

blocks.text:
4. Enforce single sign-on
Enforcing removes every other way into an account in your identity pool — passwords and linked social logins stop working. Rehearse it first: the rehearsal changes nothing and shows you exactly which accounts are affected.

screens.title: Enforce single sign-on
screens.subtitle: Rehearse, choose break-glass accounts, then enforce

blocks.text: Enforcing removes every other way into an account in your identity pool — passwords and linked social logins stop working. Rehearse it first: the rehearsal changes nothing and shows you exactly which accounts are affected.

Your organization keeps a way in that does not depend on your identity provider: {stash.ssoPreview.lockout.ownersOutsidePool.*.email} — owners who sign in outside your identity pool. Enforcement never touches those accounts, so an expired certificate or a deleted application cannot lock your organization out of itself.

{data.sso.sso.breakGlassUids:count} break-glass account(s) designated. They keep their password even after enforcement, so a lapsed certificate or a removed application in your identity provider cannot lock your organization out of itself.

Before you can enforce, your organization needs one way in that survives your identity provider failing — an expired certificate, a deleted application. Either an owner who signs in outside your identity pool (they keep their own password or social login, and enforcement never touches them), or a break-glass account inside the pool that keeps a password. Rehearse to see where you stand: without one of the two, nobody could sign in and we could not let you back in either.

blocks.title: Designated accounts that protect nothing
blocks.secondary: These hold nothing but your identity provider, so they would be locked out along with everyone else. Pick an account that also has a password.

blocks.text: No account in your identity pool can serve as break-glass: every one of them signs in through your identity provider and holds nothing else, which is exactly the credential that stops working in the situation break-glass is for. Give your organization an owner who signs in outside the pool instead — an owner whose email is not routed to your identity provider, with their own password or social login — then rehearse again. Enforcement stays unavailable until then, and the rehearsal costs nothing to re-run.

screens.title: Privacy requests
screens.subtitle: Export the people you hold, and erase one on request

blocks.text: A file of every contact this workspace holds, and one of every lead its sites captured, with the fields and the format you choose. Available on every plan, whether or not it includes the CRM.

A privacy erasure, not a delete: the person is removed from every site in this workspace, whether or not a page shows them. The request is filed now and runs with the nightly erasure job, and from the moment it is filed your sites stop capturing the address. Workspace owners and admins only.

Removed across the workspace
• The contact record on every site in this workspace — profile, notes, tags, timeline and custom fields
• Every lead for this address, on every site
• The tasks and logged activities filed against the person
• The person on any email audience list
• The campaign delivery log — every message sent to the address, with its opens and clicks

Kept, with the person taken off
• Orders and bookings stay as financial records with the name, email, phone and addresses removed
• Deals stay on the pipeline, unlinked from the person
• Companies stay, with their contact count reduced

Not reached — finish these by hand
• Form submissions — delete them from the Inbox
• A site member account — close it from the site’s Members page
